## Claims
- [source-backed] The lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- [proved] If \(r=n-r\) and \(i=j\), the conjugate parameter \(v^\vee=v_{n-r,\;n-r+j-i,\;n-r-i+1,\;n}\) equals \(v\).
- [proved] Under these hypotheses, partition conjugation induces a grading-preserving integral involution \(C:Q\to Q\), \(C([\bar s_\lambda])=[\bar s_{\lambda'}]\).
- [proved] The involution \(C\) carries \(G_L\) bijectively onto \(G_R\).

## Strategy
Put \(r=n-r\), \(i=j\), and \(b=\min(i,j)=i\). Since
\[
j=r-t+1=i,\qquad i=s-t+1,
\]
one has \(t=r-i+1\) and \(s=r\). Hence
\[
v=v_{r,r,r-i+1,2r}=v^\vee.
\]
The accepted quotient-conjugation route therefore gives an automorphism
\[
C:Q=J_v/A_+J_v\longrightarrow Q,\qquad
[\bar s_\lambda]\longmapsto[\bar s_{\lambda'}].
\]
It preserves degree since \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\), and \(C^2=1\).

Here
\[
G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^i,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq i^a\},
\qquad
G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+a)^i\}.
\]
For \(\rho\subseteq i^a\), write \(\alpha=\rho'\subseteq a^i\). Then
\[
(i^i,\rho)'=(i+\alpha_1,\ldots,i+\alpha_i),
\]
which lies in the defining interval for \(G_R\). Conversely every
\[
\mu=(i+\alpha_1,\ldots,i+\alpha_i),\qquad \alpha\subseteq a^i,
\]
has
\[
\mu'=(i^i,\alpha')\in G_L.
\]
Thus conjugation gives mutually inverse bijections \(G_L\leftrightarrow G_R\).

The requested self-conjugate corollary is established, using the accepted quotient-conjugation replacement route.
